versions.protocol_text: Farm protocol for an adult bovine with fever and reduced appetite, approved by the farm veterinarian. Supportive care, one anti-inflammatory dose by weight, notification of the veterinarian, reassessment at two hours, escalation if not improving.

steps.instructions: Take the rectal temperature again, check the skin tent for dehydration and listen for rumination.
steps.title: Confirm temperature and hydration

steps.instructions: Move the animal to shade, offer fresh water and separate it from the herd.
steps.title: Shade, water, separate

steps.instructions: One intramuscular dose of flunixin meglumine 50 mg/mL at 2.2 mg/kg (0.044 mL/kg). Not more than once in 24 hours, three doses at most.
steps.title: Flunixin meglumine by weight

steps.instructions: Send the veterinarian the temperature, the time of the dose and the animal's tag.
steps.title: Tell the veterinarian

steps.instructions: Re-take the temperature and appetite. Expect the temperature to have fallen by at least 0.5 °C.
steps.title: Reassess at two hours

steps.instructions: If the temperature is 41 °C or more, or not falling at reassessment, call the veterinarian immediately.
steps.title: Call the veterinarian now

eligibility_rules.message: This protocol is written for poultry flocks
This protocol applies to a flock, not one bird

versions.protocol_text: Flock-level heat stress: ventilation and water first, oral electrolytes in the drinking water, reassessment at one hour.

steps.instructions: Count the birds panting, check every water line and drinker is flowing.
steps.title: Count and check water

steps.instructions: Open vents, run the fans, add drinkers, stop any handling.
steps.title: Ventilation and drinkers

steps.instructions: One sachet of oral electrolyte per 10 litres of drinking water; enter the number of sachets used.
steps.title: Oral electrolytes in the water

steps.instructions: Count the birds still panting and any new deaths.
steps.title: Reassess at one hour

steps.instructions: If deaths continue or panting does not ease, call the veterinarian.
steps.title: Call the veterinarian
